correctness.rationale: PASS: For all finite nonempty connected distance-regular graphs, three-variable graph formulas can define each fixed shortest-path distance by recursively reusing the third variable (with proper binding hygiene). For necessity, an existential triple-distance formula detects any missing positive p^h_ij support bit, and a two-vertex sentence detects unequal diameter. For sufficiency, the standard three-pebble EF invariant preserves pairwise distances: with at most two old pebbles remaining, distance regularity and equality of supports guarantee a response to each new distance pair. Equality and adjacency follow from distances 0,1. For H(d,q), coordinate types a,b,c,e prove precisely binary vs >=3 alphabet separation at fixed d. Independently enumerated Hamming graphs d=1..3, q=2,3,4 and compared triple-support formulas; finite enumeration is corroboration only.
